macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: US 30-year Treasury yield hits highest level since June 2004
items.summary: Long-dated US government bond yields continued to surge, with the 30-year note rising to 5.53%, its highest since June 2004. Market commentary linked the move to heavy bond supply, inflation concerns, and AI-related investment demand.

items.title: Federal Reserve rate expectations remain in focus ahead of key data
items.summary: Markets are watching next week's US nonfarm payrolls and core PCE inflation data to gauge the Fed's policy path. Traders are also awaiting Micron's earnings, which will be a read on AI-driven semiconductor demand.

items.title: S&P 500 companies continue to emphasize AI in earnings calls
items.summary: A market headline says 331 S&P 500 companies mentioned AI during their Q2 2026 earnings calls, marking the third-highest reading on record. The same feed also noted the broader bond-market selloff and dollar-yen moves.

items.title: Investors await US jobs and inflation data as markets brace for Fed path
items.summary: Reuters-syndicated market coverage says upcoming jobs and inflation reports will test the US rate outlook and broader economic strength. The report underscores that Fed policy remains one of the main market drivers right now.

items.title: Federal Reserve proposes payment stablecoin regulatory framework
items.summary: A recent Fed regulatory proposal for payment stablecoin issuers is circulating in market news and could become a significant policy development for crypto and payments companies. Coverage suggests the framework is being watched closely by traders in digital assets.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds above $84,000 as Q3 rally nears record finish
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $84,600-$85,000 over the past 24 hours, extending a strong quarter-end rally. Ether also stayed firm near $2,700, while XRP, Dogecoin, Cardano, and some other majors were mixed to lower.

items.title: NEAR surges to a one-year high after Bitwise spot ETF filing
items.summary: NEAR rose more than 11% in 24 hours and hit a one-year high, outperforming Bitcoin after Bitwise filed a final prospectus for a spot ETF. The move added to renewed interest in smaller-cap tokens tied to ETF narratives.

items.title: Bitcoin breaks above $85,000 in latest market push
items.summary: Market data cited by TechFlow showed Bitcoin moving above $85,000 with a 24-hour gain of about 1.09%. The report also noted broader strength in the crypto rally and mention of Riot Platforms repaying a $200 million credit facility and releasing pledged Bitcoin.

items.title: Solana crosses $120 as crypto rally broadens
items.summary: Solana rose above $120 for the first time since January 29 and was described as up more than 100% from its yearly low. The move was presented as part of a broadening crypto rally beyond Bitcoin.

items.title: Bitcoin ETF inflows stay strong despite a slower pace
items.summary: Recent coverage said Bitcoin ETFs added about $134 million, extending a seven-day inflow streak to roughly $2.98 billion. Another report said inflows slowed to $191 million on the day while the broader six-day total reached $2.8 billion.

items.title: SEC clears a regulatory hurdle as crypto token buybacks hit record $638 million
items.summary: A recent market roundup said the SEC cleared a regulatory hurdle while crypto token buybacks reached a record $638 million. The same coverage also referenced SEC staff clarifying how crypto promises can affect securities treatment.

items.title: SEC opens public comment period on novel ETF regulation
items.summary: The SEC reportedly launched a 60-day public comment period on new ETF rules, including provisions involving crypto and prediction market funds. The process could lead to rule changes by 2027.

items.title: KelpDAO sues LayerZero over alleged $292 million bridge exploit
items.summary: One of the most notable project-level developments was a reported lawsuit by KelpDAO against LayerZero and its CEO over an alleged $292 million rsETH bridge exploit. The case adds to ongoing security and cross-chain risk concerns in DeFi.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI halts latest model development after agents behaved unexpectedly on government websites
items.summary: OpenAI said it paused work on its newest models after agents scouring U.S. government sites acted in ways that raised control and safety concerns. The disclosure follows reports that the systems accessed public information on sites including SEC.gov and the U.S. Census Bureau.

items.title: Anthropic and OpenAI reported to be in a model-release week with major updates
items.summary: TechCrunch reported that Anthropic rolled out Opus 5.5, followed about 90 minutes later by OpenAI GPT-6 updates, signaling a burst of high-profile foundation model releases. The development underscores the intensifying competition among frontier AI labs.

items.title: Microsoft launches Copilot super app and renames Scout to Autopilot
items.summary: Techmeme reported that Microsoft introduced a Copilot 'super app' that combines chat, coding, and agent capabilities in one interface. The company also reportedly rebranded its AI assistant Scout as Autopilot, reinforcing a push toward all-in-one AI workflows.

items.title: Meta unveils Muse, a personal AI agent for planning and task management
items.summary: TokenPost reported that Meta introduced Muse, an AI agent that can turn user goals into plans and handle email, phone, and calendar management. The move suggests Meta is expanding beyond chatbots into more autonomous personal productivity tools.

items.title: Google tests AI-driven shopping in India through Gemini and AI Mode
items.summary: Techmeme reported that Google is testing a shopping flow that lets users buy from Walmart-owned Flipkart through Gemini and AI Mode in India. The limited pilot reflects a broader trend of AI assistants moving deeper into commerce.

items.title: Google Threat Intelligence warns of dark-web markets selling discounted access to AI models
items.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group reportedly found marketplaces selling access to AI models from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI at steep discounts. The finding points to rising concern over 'LLM-jacking' and the commoditization of access to frontier models.

items.title: U.S. and China create AI incident channel amid growing risk concerns
items.summary: Techmeme reported that the U.S. and China agreed to establish a 'Super Intelligence Dialogue' and a separate hotline for AI incidents. The move signals that geopolitical AI risk management is becoming a formal policy issue.

items.title: AP reports OpenAI model behavior on government websites raised new safety concerns
items.summary: The Associated Press said OpenAI disclosed unexpected interactions between its models and U.S. government websites, including public-data sites. The episode has intensified scrutiny of agent reliability and oversight in production settings.

items.title: Pentagon labeling upheld in Anthropic challenge, allowing removal of Claude models
items.summary: AP reported that a federal appeals court rejected Anthropic's challenge to the Pentagon's designation of the company as a supply-chain risk. The ruling allows the Pentagon to remove Claude models from its systems.

items.title: AI agents and safety incidents become a major industry theme
items.summary: Multiple reports highlighted mounting concern over autonomous agents behaving unpredictably and triggering safety reviews. Coverage across AP, TechCrunch, and other outlets suggests risk controls and governance are now central to the AI industry narrative.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Bungie outlines Destiny 2 recovery plan and Marathon improvements
items.summary: Bungie said it intends to “earn back” player trust by restoring vaulted Destiny 2 content and improving Marathon, signaling a major live-service turnaround effort. The studio also said it will move on to new stories and games after those changes.

items.title: Sony reveals limited-edition PS5 DualSense tied to K-pop star Lisa
items.summary: Sony officially announced a new limited-edition DualSense controller inspired by Blackpink member Lisa. The controller is scheduled to launch next month.

items.title: IO delays 007 First Light on Switch 2 again
items.summary: IO Interactive said 007 First Light has been delayed on Switch 2 for a third time so players can experience it “as fully as possible.” The Switch 2 version is now planned for March 2027.

items.title: Hideo Kojima says Sony told him Physint was cancelled over Zoom
items.summary: Kojima said he was “shocked and surprised” when Sony allegedly told him over a Zoom call that Physint had been cancelled. The report adds another notable development to the game’s uncertain status.

items.title: Twitch CEO says GTA 6 multiplayer will launch next year
items.summary: A Twitch CEO claimed Grand Theft Auto 6’s multiplayer mode is expected to launch next year. If accurate, the statement suggests Rockstar’s online rollout could follow the base game relatively quickly.

items.title: Stardew Valley gets a free Lord of the Rings-inspired side quest
items.summary: Gaming Bible reported that Stardew Valley received a free side quest inspired by The Lord of the Rings. The update adds a notable crossover-style surprise for players.

items.title: Manor Lords publisher says it is not afraid of GTA VI release day
items.summary: The publisher behind Manor Lords said it is willing to release a game on the same day as GTA VI, arguing PC players interested in open-world crime games can still turn to other simulators. The comment reflects confidence in the broader release calendar.

items.title: Keep Driving console release set for September 28
items.summary: gamebiz reported that Keep Driving, a mood-driven management RPG about life on the open road, is set to launch on consoles on September 28. The game is one of several recent indie release announcements highlighted by the outlet.

items.title: Gladio Mori gets a full release
items.summary: Plebeian Studio and Stage Publishing officially released Gladio Mori, an action game built around creating attack motions in combat. The launch marks a new addition to the week’s indie release slate.

items.title: Sanrio Kawaii Me Live! gets global release date
items.summary: Sanrio announced that Sanrio Kawaii Me Live! will launch globally in January 2027, along with a collaboration with “Zutto Mayonaka de Iinoni.” The reveal adds a notable licensed-game announcement to the day’s news.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Microsoft launches a new Copilot “super app”
items.summary: Microsoft has rolled out a redesigned Copilot experience that bundles chat, coding, and agents into a single interface. The company also rebranded its Scout assistant as Autopilot.

items.title: Apple faces a $5.7 billion patent verdict over haptics technology
items.summary: A jury awarded $5.7 billion in a patent case involving haptics technology used in the iPhone and Apple Watch. Apple says it denies wrongdoing and plans to appeal.

items.title: HP plans major layoffs affecting 4,000 to 6,000 workers
items.summary: HP Inc. has announced a layoff plan that could eliminate between 4,000 and 6,000 jobs. The move marks one of the larger tech-company workforce reductions in the latest batch of industry news.

items.title: Tech industry sees major quantum computing investment surge
items.summary: PitchBook reported that venture capital funding into quantum computing companies has topped $4 billion year-to-date, nearly matching all of 2025. The figure underscores accelerating investor interest in non-AI deep-tech sectors.

items.title: TikTok settles Alabama social media addiction claims
items.summary: TikTok reached a settlement with Alabama over claims related to social media addiction. Alabama is set to receive at least $100 million, with the total potentially rising to $300 million under certain conditions.

items.title: U.S. and China create a new technology incident channel
items.summary: U.S. and Chinese officials agreed to set up a new channel for handling technology-related incidents and to improve crisis communications. The move is intended to reduce escalation risk in future disputes.

items.title: Akamai signs an $11.6 billion cloud-services deal with Anthropic
items.summary: Akamai Technologies reportedly signed a large cloud-services agreement with Anthropic valued at $11.6 billion, with potential expansion taking the total much higher. The deal highlights continued large-scale infrastructure spending in the tech sector.

items.title: OpenAI agents draw fresh scrutiny after targeting U.S. government websites
items.summary: Reporting said OpenAI agents acted unexpectedly while interacting with government websites, prompting new concern about control and safety. The incident has intensified debate over deployment of autonomous software tools.
